name: servicenow-docs
description: Search the official ServiceNow product docs (Australia and Brazil releases) from Claude, with cited answers.
long_description:
Gives Claude three read-only tools over the official ServiceNow product documentation (Australia and Brazil releases): **snow_docs_search** (semantic + keyword search with reranking, over an index where every passage carries a short context line — the retrieval setup that measured best), **snow_docs_read** (the full section behind a result) and **snow_docs_status**. Claude answers from the returned passages and cites them.

Everything runs on your computer. The first launch downloads the docs index (~550 MB) from GitHub and two small search models (~1.2 GB) from Hugging Face; after that it works offline. Needs ~2.6 GB of disk and about 3 GB of RAM once it has answered a search. Runs on Windows 10/11 (x64), macOS 14+ on Apple silicon and Linux. Uses uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to set up Python; install it first if Claude Desktop reports that the server failed to start.

tools.name: snow_docs_search
tools.description: Search the official ServiceNow product documentation; returns cited passages.

tools.name: snow_docs_read
tools.description: Read the full documentation section behind a search result.

tools.name: snow_docs_status
tools.description: Show setup progress, the docs snapshot served, and where data is stored.

prompts.name: answer
prompts.description: Answer a ServiceNow question from the official docs, with citations.
prompts.text:
You have tools for the official ServiceNow product documentation, for the australia and brazil
releases (snow_docs_search's `release` argument; australia unless the user's instance runs brazil).
When answering a ServiceNow question with them:
1. Call snow_docs_search first, with the query in English using ServiceNow's own terms: the docs
   are English-only, so translate a question asked in another language (and still answer in
   the user's language). Rephrase and search again if results look off-topic or weak.
2. Answer ONLY from the passages the tools returned; do not fill gaps from memory.
3. Cite every factual claim with the passage id in square brackets, e.g. [australia:markdown/...md::Heading]; when a result has a url, you may also link it.
4. Before giving step-by-step instructions, call snow_docs_read on the id to get the full section.
5. If the docs do not cover the question, or only cover a different release or product, say so plainly.
6. If two sources disagree, point out the conflict and cite both.

Question: ${arguments.question}

data_folder.title: Data folder
data_folder.description: Where the docs index (~1.3 GB) and search models (~1.2 GB) are kept. Claude Code installs of this server use the same default folder, so the download happens once.
